**Proof.**

Write $h = \dfrac 1 2 \paren{f + g + \size{f - g}}$. By the definitions of pointwise addition, pointwise difference, absolute value of a real-valued function, and pointwise scalar multiplication, $h$ is the mapping $S \to \R$ given by
$$\forall s \in S: \quad h(s) = \tfrac12\bigl(f(s) + g(s) + |f(s) - g(s)|\bigr).$$
Both $f \vee g$ and $h$ are mappings with domain $S$ and codomain $\R$, so by equality of mappings it suffices to show $(f \vee g)(s) = h(s)$ for every $s \in S$.

Fix $s \in S$ and put $a = f(s)$, $b = g(s)$, real numbers. We show $\max\{a,b\} = \tfrac12(a + b + |a-b|)$. By totality of the ordering of $\R$, either $a \ge b$ or $a < b$.

*Case $a \ge b$.* Then $\max\{a,b\} = a$ and $a - b \ge 0$, so $|a-b| = a-b$. Hence
$$\tfrac12(a + b + |a-b|) = \tfrac12(a + b + a - b) = \tfrac12(2a) = a = \max\{a,b\}.$$

*Case $a < b$.* Then $\max\{a,b\} = b$ and $a - b < 0$, so $|a-b| = -(a-b) = b-a$. Hence
$$\tfrac12(a + b + |a-b|) = \tfrac12(a + b + b - a) = \tfrac12(2b) = b = \max\{a,b\}.$$

In both cases $(f\vee g)(s) = \max\{f(s), g(s)\} = h(s)$. Since $s \in S$ was arbitrary, $f \vee g = h = \dfrac 1 2 \paren{f + g + \size{f - g}}$. (If $S = \varnothing$, both are the empty mapping and the statement holds trivially; the argument above covers this vacuously.) $\blacksquare$
